title: The Secret Sauce for Promotion Decisions
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that competency frameworks, while useful, aren't sufficient for making sound promotion decisions, especially into senior leadership roles. It proposes adding explicit 'standards' - qualitative, ongoing expectations of how someone shows up - as a complement to skills-based competencies. Unlike competencies, which can be checked off a list, standards are never fully achieved; they describe a level of conduct and contribution that must be continually earned. Making these standards explicit, the author argues, helps both decision-makers and candidates understand what's genuinely being evaluated when promotions are on the line, replacing vague, unspoken judgments with clearer expectations.
points: Competency checklists alone are not enough to make sound senior promotion decisions.
The article proposes adding qualitative 'standards' that describe ongoing conduct, not a one-time skill.
Standards, unlike competencies, are never fully completed - they must be earned continuously.
Naming these standards explicitly helps candidates understand what's really being judged.
Combining competencies with clear standards gives leaders more confidence in promotion calls.
quotes: Deciding who is ready for more leadership responsibility... is a decision that often defines many teams and organizations.
Leaders naturally turn to the unspoken “stuff” they believe makes the difference when assessing the true merits of a colleague.
Unlike competencies, standards reflect a level of quality attainment rather than a skill or talent.
Transparency in the standards leaders use to consider promotion allows colleagues to strive for a higher level of performance
